103.body:
ComputePartitionStatistics writes a Parquet statistics file for the transaction's current branch head and stages its registration. Use a fresh transaction and commit it to publish the reference: txn := tbl.NewTransaction()
stats, err := txn.ComputePartitionStatistics(ctx)
if err != nil { /* ... */ }
newTbl, err := txn.Commit(ctx) The operation recomputes statistics from live manifest entries without reading data files, delete-file contents, or Puffin blobs. It groups rows by partition spec ID and partition tuple and sorts by the unified tuple with NULL first. V2 includes position and equality delete metrics. V3 also counts deletion vectors in dv_count; their records contribute to position_delete_record_count, while position_delete_file_count counts classic files only, including V2 files retained after an upgrade. total_record_count is exact for tables without deletes and for DV-only tables whose live targets, partitions, sequence numbers, and record counts can be validated from metadata. A live classic position or equality delete makes this field NULL for every partition, since deletes may apply across specs. Unknown DV sequence numbers also leave the affected total NULL. Optional last-updated fields are left NULL. PartitionStatisticsSchema exposes the versioned schema; PartitionStatisticsSchemaV1 remains available. The table must have a snapshot and at least one partition field in its spec history. Dropped partition source fields and changed transform result types are not supported. A concurrent change to the target branch, current schema, or partition layout rejects the commit. Statistics do not create a new snapshot.
103.title: Partition statistics (v1-v3)

104.body: puffin.Writer.AddBlob accepts BlobMetadataInput.CompressionCodec with CompressionCodecLZ4 or CompressionCodecZstd. puffin.Reader.ReadBlob decodes the stored codec. Pass 0 for the current snapshot. Omit the column names to analyze all supported top-level primitive columns in the snapshot schema. Geometry, geography, and unknown types are skipped by default. Explicit column names must refer to supported top-level primitive columns. The estimates exclude null values and empty strings and binary values. After writing a Puffin statistics file, pass its snapshot ID, path, sizes, and blob metadata to txn.SetStatistics. 111.body: variant is the Iceberg v3 semi-structured type: a single self-describing column that holds arbitrary JSON-like values (objects, arrays, and scalars) without a fixed schema. iceberg-go supports both non-shredded and shredded variants, and can push predicates down into individual variant fields.
111.title: Variant Type

112.body:
A variant column is declared with iceberg.VariantType{} in the table schema and maps to the Arrow variant extension type (see API ). Non-shredded variant values need no extra configuration: write an Arrow record whose variant column uses the extension type, and read it back the same way. Build the column with a variant builder and write it like any other Arrow column (the table must be format version 3): import ( "fmt" "github.com/apache/arrow-go/v18/arrow" "github.com/apache/arrow-go/v18/arrow/array" "github.com/apache/arrow-go/v18/arrow/extensions" "github.com/apache/arrow-go/v18/arrow/memory" "github.com/apache/arrow-go/v18/parquet/variant" "github.com/apache/iceberg-go" "github.com/apache/iceberg-go/table"
) // tbl was created with table.PropertyFormatVersion = "3" and this schema.
schema := iceberg.NewSchema(0, iceberg.NestedField{ID: 1, Name: "payload", Type: iceberg.VariantType{}},
)
arrowSchema, _ := table.SchemaToArrowSchema(schema, nil, true, false) bldr := extensions.NewVariantBuilder(memory.DefaultAllocator, extensions.NewDefaultVariantType())
defer bldr.Release() var vb variant.Builder
_ = vb.Append(map[string]any{"x": int64(320), "target": "button-submit"})
val, _ := vb.Build()
bldr.Append(val) col := bldr.NewArray()
defer col.Release()
rec := array.NewRecordBatch(arrowSchema, []arrow.Array{col}, 1)
defer rec.Release() tx := tbl.NewTransaction()
arrTable := array.NewTableFromRecords(arrowSchema, []arrow.Record{rec})
defer arrTable.Release()
_ = tx.AppendTable(ctx, arrTable, 1024, nil)
tbl, _ = tx.Commit(ctx) A normal scan reads it back; the variant column comes back as an *extensions.VariantArray: result, _ := tbl.Scan().ToArrowTable(ctx)
defer result.Release() variants := result.Column(0).Data().Chunk(0).(*extensions.VariantArray)
v, _ := variants.Value(0)
fmt.Println(v.Value()) // variant.ObjectValue for the object above

113.body: Shredding stores the fields of a variant as typed Parquet sub-columns instead of a single opaque blob. This lets scans read and filter a field as a native column rather than decoding every value. Shredding is opt-in and configured with two write properties (see Configuration ): write.parquet.shred-variants - enable shredding of top-level variant columns (default false). write.parquet.variant-inference-buffer-size - rows buffered per file to infer the shredding schema (default 100). The reader accepts both shredded and non-shredded data; no read-side configuration is required.

124.body:
iceberg.Extract(ref, path, typ) builds a term that navigates a member-selector path into a variant column and casts the leaf to typ. The path uses dot ($.user.age) or quoted-bracket ($['user']['age']) notation; array indexing ($.items[0]), wildcards, filters, and recursive descent are rejected at bind time. It is an UnboundTerm, so it plugs into the same predicate builders as iceberg.Reference: filter := iceberg.EqualTo( iceberg.Extract(iceberg.Reference("payload"), "$.user.age", iceberg.PrimitiveTypes.Int64), int64(30),
) The referenced column must be a variant, and a target type is required. Supported target types: bool, int32, int64, float32, float64, date, time, timestamp, timestamptz, timestamp_ns, timestamptz_ns, string, fixed, binary, decimal, uuid. Caveats: Extract predicates prune whole data files by shredded-field bounds (best-effort, and only for shredded fields), then filter row by row. Row-group statistics and bloom filters do not apply to them. Extract terms are DSL-only (no string row-filter form) and are not REST-serializable. Under local scan planning (the default) they run as local residuals; with remote scan planning, a filter containing an Extract term fails to serialize rather than being silently dropped. See Variant Type for shredding.

The iceberg CLI loads catalog defaults from ~/.iceberg-go.yaml (override the directory with GOICEBERG_HOME). The schema, defined in config/config.go , is: default-catalog: default
max-workers: 5
catalog: default: type: rest uri: https://example.com/iceberg warehouse: s3://my-bucket/warehouse credential: <client-id>:<client-secret> output: text aws-profile: "" rest: sigv4-enabled: false signing-name: "" signing-region: "" Key Purpose default-catalog Name used when --catalog-name is not passed on the CLI. max-workers Worker pool size for concurrent operations. Default 5. catalog.<name>.type One of rest, hive, glue, sql, hadoop, dynamodb. catalog.<name>.uri Catalog endpoint or DSN. catalog.<name>.warehouse Warehouse identifier (REST/Glue) or location (Hive/SQL). catalog.<name>.credential Credential string passed through to the catalog's auth handler. catalog.<name>.output CLI output format (e.g. text, json). catalog.<name>.aws-profile AWS named profile for Glue and DynamoDB catalogs. When unset, the AWS SDK default credential chain is used. catalog.<name>.sql-driver database/sql driver name for the SQL catalog. Maps to the sql.driver property. The default CLI binary only compiles in sqliteshim; other drivers require a custom build. catalog.<name>.sql-dialect SQL dialect for the SQL catalog (postgres, mysql, sqlite, mssql, oracle). Maps to the sql.dialect property. The default CLI binary only ships sqlite via sqliteshim; other dialects need a custom build with their drivers. catalog.<name>.rest.sigv4-enabled Enable AWS SigV4 signing for REST. 131.body:
A term is the left-hand side of a predicate. Iceberg-go has two flavors: Reference("column_name") - an unbound term that names a column (exprs.go:373). Typing happens at bind time, when the expression is matched against a schema. This is what you almost always want. BoundReference - the resolved form, produced by Reference.Bind(schema, caseSensitive) (exprs.go:389). You only encounter these when writing custom expression visitors. Extract(ref, path, typ) - a variant sub-path term that navigates a member-selector path ($.a.b or $['a']['b']; no array indexing or wildcards) into a variant column and casts the leaf to typ (variant_extract.go). Use it inside any predicate builder to filter on a field within a variant. See Row Filter Syntax . The interfaces are: type Term interface { ... } // shared marker
type UnboundTerm interface { Term; ... } // pre-bind
type BoundTerm interface { Term; Ref() BoundReference; ... } (exprs.go:317-348)

142.body: A retry replays staged changes in order against the refreshed table. It replans each ExpireSnapshots call at its original position, with the original options and cutoff time. The plan retains snapshots that a concurrent commit made reachable, such as rollback targets and new branch heads. It can expire snapshots that a concurrent append moved outside the retention window. A transaction that appends and expires snapshots rebases onto a concurrent append like any other append. Each attempt requires the refs read by expiries that remove snapshots or refs to be unchanged since loading or refreshing the table. An expiry that removes nothing adds no such requirement. If a concurrent commit moves one of those refs before the attempt succeeds, it causes another conflict. The next attempt replans the expiry. If a concurrent commit creates a ref that the plan did not read, that ref does not cause a conflict. Expiring its snapshot also removes the ref. Retries replan an expiry even if staging or an earlier attempt produced no expiry updates. A retry stamps snapshots staged earlier in the transaction after the expiry's cutoff, so the retry keeps them even if the staged plan expired them. If no updates remain, for example because a concurrent commit already expired the same snapshots, Commit returns the refreshed table without committing. A transaction containing only expiries with no updates makes no commit attempt and never refreshes or replans. Post-commit cleanup deletes files for snapshots expired by the successful attempt, if cleanup is enabled. A retry fails with ErrTransactionUnusable if GC is disabled after refresh, a staged change no longer applies, or replanning changes whether a non-main commit branch is removed. ErrTransactionUnusable and ErrCommitFailed list these cases and which of them a new transaction can retry.

143.body: Iceberg Go implements Iceberg's Metrics Reporting API. After scan planning it can emit a ScanReport (files and manifests considered, scanned, and skipped; bytes read; planning duration), and after a commit a CommitReport (commit attempts, duration, and the added/removed/total file, record, and delete counts). These metrics are otherwise invisible from outside the client; a reporter gives operators a standard way to collect them. A pluggable metrics.Reporter is the sink that receives those reports. The skipped-data-files and skipped-delete-files counters track file entries rejected by partition or metrics filters in manifests the planner reads. The skipped-manifest counters track pruning at the earlier manifest level.
143.title: Metrics Reporting

144.body: Reporting is strictly opt-in . With no reporter configured the instrumented code paths do no work, and the client emits no logs and no network traffic. This is a deliberate divergence from Iceberg Java, which defaults to the logging reporter. A library must not start emitting output the caller never asked for, so Iceberg Go defaults to a no-op reporter until you select one. Callers migrating from Java that want reports by default must select the logging reporter explicitly.

Experimental. The OpenTelemetry metric and attribute names track the still-unmerged Iceberg Java reporter ( apache/iceberg#16250 ) and may change to stay aligned with it. The metrics/otel package provides an OpenTelemetry-backed reporter. The host owns the OpenTelemetry SDK; the reporter only looks up a meter (the global MeterProvider by default, or one you pass with WithMeter). import "github.com/apache/iceberg-go/metrics/otel" rep, err := otel.NewReporter( otel.WithMeter(meter), otel.WithAttributes(otel.AttrTableName, otel.AttrOperation),
) It exports a curated subset of the report fields under iceberg.scan.* / iceberg.commit.* instrument names (e.g. iceberg.scan.planning.duration, iceberg.scan.result.data_files, iceberg.commit.duration, iceberg.commit.data_files.added). Instrument types follow the meaning of each field. Durations are histograms (in milliseconds). The commit *.total fields (iceberg.commit.records.total, iceberg.commit.data_files.total, iceberg.commit.delete_files.total, iceberg.commit.file_size.total_bytes, iceberg.commit.positional_deletes.total and iceberg.commit.equality_deletes.total) describe the table after the commit, so they are gauges that hold the last reported value; do not sum them over time. Everything else (added/removed deltas, attempts, manifest stats and all scan fields) is a monotonic counter. Gauges are last-write-wins per attribute set, so dropping the table name from WithAttributes makes different tables overwrite each other's totals. WithAttributes bounds label cardinality by allowlist. The default set is table name + operation; schema id (otel.AttrSchemaID) is opt-in. The snapshot id is never attached as a metric attribute because it is unbounded — per-snapshot detail stays available through the full reports and the table's snapshot history. The OpenTelemetry reporter is not registered under a metrics-reporter-impl name automatically. To select it by property, register a factory for it as shown in Writing a custom reporter ; otherwise pass the instance to table.WithReporter or table.WithMetricsReporter.

166.body: Before starting work on an issue: Check for existing PRs. Search the open pull requests to make sure nobody is already working on it. Claim the issue. Leave a comment on the issue (e.g., "I'd like to work on this") and wait for a maintainer to acknowledge before writing code. One at a time for new contributors. If you haven't had a PR merged into iceberg-go yet, please work on one issue at a time. Get it reviewed, address feedback, get it merged — then pick up the next one. This helps us give your work the attention it deserves and avoids wasted effort from overlapping contributions. If two PRs land for the same issue, we will generally keep the one from the contributor who claimed it first.
166.title: Picking Up Issues

167.body: Reference the issue number in your PR description (e.g., "Fixes #123"). Keep PRs focused — one issue per PR. Run make test and make lint before pushing. CI runs all of these too, but catching issues locally saves a round-trip. make lint-install will install the linter if you don't have it yet. All commits must have a Signed-off-by line ( DCO ). CI checks the exported API against the base branch with apidiff. If your PR changes it incompatibly on purpose, mark the PR title as breaking with a !, for example refactor(io)!: add context to IO.Open. You can run the same check locally with dev/check-api-compat.sh after installing the apidiff version it names.
167.title: Submitting a Pull Request

176.body: This glossary defines important terms used throughout the Iceberg ecosystem, organized in tables for easy reference.
176.title: Glossary

177.body: Term Definition Catalog A centralized service that manages table metadata and provides a unified interface for accessing Iceberg tables. Catalogs can be implemented as Hive metastore, AWS Glue, REST API, or SQL-based solutions. Table A collection of data files organized by a schema, with metadata tracking changes over time through snapshots. Tables support ACID transactions and schema evolution. Schema The structure definition of a table, specifying field names, types, and whether fields are required or optional. Schemas are versioned and can evolve over time. Snapshot A point-in-time view of a table's data, representing the state after a specific operation (append, overwrite, delete, etc.). Each snapshot contains metadata about the operation and references to data files. Manifest A metadata file that lists data files and their metadata (location, partition information, record counts, etc.). Manifests are organized into manifest lists for efficient access. Manifest List A file that contains references to manifest files for a specific snapshot, enabling efficient discovery of data files without reading all manifests.
177.title: Core Concepts

181.body: Operation Description Append An operation that adds new data files to a table without removing existing data. Creates a new snapshot with the additional files. Overwrite An operation that replaces existing data files with new ones, typically based on a partition predicate. Creates a new snapshot with the replacement files. Delete An operation that removes data files from a table, either by marking them as deleted or by removing references to them. Replace An operation that completely replaces all data in a table with new data, typically used for full table refreshes.
181.title: Operations

182.body: Term Definition Partition A logical division of table data based on column values, used to improve query performance by allowing selective reading of relevant data files. Partition Spec Defines how table data is partitioned by specifying source columns and transformations (identity, bucket, truncate, year, month, day, hour). Partition Field A field in the partition spec that defines how a source column is transformed for partitioning. Partition Path The file system path structure created by partition values, typically in the format partition_name=value/.
182.title: Partitioning

183.body: Transform Description identity Use the column value directly bucket[n] Hash the value into n buckets truncate[n] Truncate strings to n characters year Extract year from date/timestamp month Extract month from date/timestamp day Extract day from date/timestamp hour Extract hour from timestamp void Always returns null (used for unpartitioned tables)
183.title: Partition Transforms

184.body: Term Definition Expression A computation or comparison that can be evaluated against table data, used for filtering and transformations. Predicate A boolean expression used to filter data, such as column comparisons, null checks, or set membership tests. Bound Predicate A predicate that has been resolved against a specific schema, with field references bound to actual columns. Unbound Predicate A predicate that contains unresolved field references, typically in string form before binding to a schema. Literal A constant value used in expressions and predicates, such as numbers, strings, dates, etc.
184.title: Expressions and Predicates

185.body: Format Usage Description Parquet Data files The primary data file format used by Iceberg, providing columnar storage with compression and encoding optimizations. Avro Metadata files Used for manifests and manifest lists due to its schema evolution capabilities and compact binary format. ORC Data files An alternative columnar format supported by some Iceberg implementations.
185.title: File Formats

186.body: Term Definition Metadata File A JSON file containing table metadata including schema, partition spec, properties, and snapshot information. Metadata Location The URI pointing to the current metadata file for a table, stored in the catalog. Properties Key-value pairs that configure table behavior, such as compression settings, write options, and custom metadata. Statistics Metadata about data files including record counts, file sizes, and value ranges for optimization.
186.title: Metadata

187.body: Term Definition Transaction A sequence of operations that are committed atomically, ensuring data consistency and ACID properties. Commit The process of finalizing a transaction by creating a new snapshot and updating the metadata file. Rollback The process of undoing changes in a transaction, typically by reverting to a previous snapshot.
187.title: Transactions

188.body: Term Definition Branch A named reference to a specific snapshot, allowing multiple concurrent views of table data. Tag An immutable reference to a specific snapshot, typically used for versioning and releases.
188.title: References

189.body: Term Definition Warehouse The root directory or bucket where table data and metadata are stored. Location Provider A component that generates file paths for table data and metadata based on table location and naming conventions. FileIO An abstraction layer for reading and writing files across different storage systems (local filesystem, S3, GCS, Azure Blob, etc.).

190.body: Technique Description Column Pruning A technique that reads only the columns needed for a query, reducing I/O and improving performance. Partition Pruning A technique that skips reading data files from irrelevant partitions based on query predicates. Predicate Pushdown A technique that applies filtering predicates at the storage layer, reducing data transfer and processing. Statistics-based Optimization Using table and file statistics to optimize query execution plans and file selection.
190.title: Query Optimization

191.body: Term Definition Schema Evolution The process of modifying a table's schema over time while maintaining backward compatibility. Column Addition Adding new columns to a table schema, which are typically optional to maintain compatibility. Column Deletion Removing columns from a table schema, which may be logical (marking as deleted) or physical. Column Renaming Changing column names while preserving data and type information. Type Evolution Changing column types in ways that maintain data compatibility (e.g., int32 to int64).
191.title: Schema Evolution

192.body: Term Definition Time Travel The ability to query a table as it existed at a specific point in time using snapshot timestamps. Snapshot Isolation A property that ensures queries see a consistent view of data as it existed at a specific snapshot.
192.title: Time Travel

193.body: Property Description Atomicity Ensures that all operations in a transaction either succeed completely or fail completely. Consistency Ensures that the table remains in a valid state after each transaction. Isolation Ensures that concurrent transactions do not interfere with each other. Durability Ensures that committed changes are permanently stored and survive system failures.

198.body: AddDataFiles and AddDataFilesByPath no longer add a file twice on retry. When a commit retry finds that a concurrent commit already added one of the same paths, the commit now fails with table.ErrDuplicateDataFiles, which also matches table.ErrTransactionUnusable. Previously, the retry added the file a second time and scans returned its rows twice. With WithoutDuplicateCheck or ignoreDuplicates=true, the retry still adds the file again, as before. gocloud types are no longer exposed by blobfs and gcs. blobfs.New now returns the blobfs.FileIO interface, which lists the iceberg-go io interfaces and io.Closer, instead of a struct that embeds *blob.Bucket. FileIO.NewWriter, blobfs.Writer and gcs.ParseGCSConfig are removed; use Create, or configure GCS through properties. To migrate, replace *blobfs.FileIO with blobfs.FileIO in fields, signatures and var _ X = (*blobfs.FileIO)(nil) assertions, and assert Sys() results to blobfs.FileIO instead of *blobfs.FileIO. Catalog and view FileIO may use isolated registries. Glue, Hadoop, Hive and SQL accept WithIORegistry, as REST already does. hadoop.NewCatalog, sql.NewCatalog, view.CreateView, view.CreateViewWithIOProperties, view.CreateViewFromVersion and view.WriteMetadata now take a trailing variadic option. Existing calls still compile. Function values assigned to a type with the old signature need a wrapper that calls the function without options. The default remains the global registry, including for catalog.Load. RowDelta.Commit can be called once per builder. A second Commit on the same RowDelta now returns an error wrapping table.ErrInvalidOperation and stages nothing, even if the first call failed, as RewriteFiles.Commit does. Previously, calling Commit again after a failed first call could succeed, and calling it again after a successful one staged the builder's files a second time. Create a new builder with Transaction.NewRowDelta for each commit. Data-file replacements now reject concurrent deletes. Commits staged through ReplaceDataFiles, ReplaceDataFilesByPath, ReplaceFiles, or rewrite operations can return table.ErrConflictingDeleteFiles when a concurrent position delete targets a replaced file or any concurrent equality delete is added. Compaction on tables with streaming equality deletes may see additional conflicts. Orphan cleanup now rejects gc.enabled=false. DeleteOrphanFiles, PlanOrphanFiles, ExecuteOrphanCleanup, and dry runs now return an error before filesystem access. The iceberg clean-orphan-files command is also affected. Orphan cleanup requires complete snapshot history. DeleteOrphanFiles, PlanOrphanFiles, ExecuteOrphanCleanup, dry runs, and iceberg clean-orphan-files now reject tables loaded with REST snapshot-loading-mode=refs, returning an error wrapping table.ErrInvalidOperation. Configure the REST catalog with snapshot-loading-mode=all (or omit it) and reload the table; a server override that forces refs prevents cleanup through that catalog. maintenance.PurgeFiles is unaffected. Partition specs reject source types a transform cannot handle. Creating or updating a spec with an incompatible source, such as day(string), now fails. Writes to existing incompatible specs return ErrInvalidTransform instead of writing null partition values. REST CreateTable validates the partition spec locally. Invalid specs, including transforms with incompatible source types, return an error matching iceberg.ErrInvalidPartitionSpec before the create request. Previously, the server could return rest.ErrBadRequest. New partition specs reject multiple sources for built-in transforms. Create-table and add-spec payloads with this shape return ErrInvalidPartitionSpec. Historical metadata with such a field still loads and round-trips, but the field is skipped during partition pruning and residual simplification. Multi-source unknown transforms remain supported. Unsigned partition values no longer wrap. Partitioned writes accept the full Arrow uint32 range for Iceberg long sources and return iceberg.ErrInvalidArgument when an unsigned value exceeds the destination’s signed range. Invalid name mappings now stop scans and add-files. Tables with an unparseable schema.name-mapping.default now return ErrInvalidMetadata on scans and add-files instead of ignoring the mapping. Fix the property with a valid mapping or remove it. SigV4 keeps the token or credential as Original-Authorization. With rest.sigv4-enabled=true (or rest.auth.type=sigv4) and a token or credential, requests used to be signed with the token silently dropped, because the SigV4 signature replaced the Authorization header. They now carry it as Original-Authorization, included in the signed headers, as Iceberg Java does. A server behind SigV4 that ignores the header is unaffected. Float and double literal comparators use Iceberg ordering. TypedLiteral.Comparator() now orders -0.0 before +0.0 and NaN after all other values; NaN compares equal to NaN. Callers that use these public comparators may see a different order or equality result. Table creation rejects duplicate field IDs. NewMetadata, and CreateTable on catalogs that build metadata through it (not REST), now return ErrInvalidSchema when two fields in the schema share an ID, including unset 0 or -1 IDs, even for unpartitioned, unsorted tables. Before, the partition spec or sort order could bind to the wrong column. Callers should assign unique IDs (or let the schema be built with fresh IDs). This matches Java, whose Schema constructor rejects duplicate IDs. Struct defaults must be empty objects. Non-null initial-default and write-default values for struct fields must be {}; defaults for nested fields belong on those fields. Tables with populated struct defaults written by older iceberg-go versions still load, but AddSchema validates the entire resulting schema. Any schema update, including one that changes an unrelated column, will fail until the populated default is cleared. Schemas with duplicate field IDs are rejected. Table and view metadata now fail to load with ErrInvalidSchema if any schema in their history has two fields sharing an ID, including 0 or -1; Java Iceberg already rejects these. Older releases could write such schemas through SQL CreateView, view.CreateView or view.NewMetadata, or through CommitTable with NewAddSchemaUpdate on non-REST catalogs, when IDs were left unset; these calls, and the new UpdateView, now return ErrInvalidSchema instead. To recover, drop and recreate an affected view. For a table, point the catalog at a copy of the metadata without that schema through an atomic catalog metadata replacement, instead of editing the currently referenced metadata file in place. Sort order replacements reuse orders staged earlier in the same transaction. If a transaction replaces order A with B and then returns to A, A becomes the default again instead of B. The final update reuses A's ID instead of adding another definition. Reuse of orders from earlier commits was already supported. Case-insensitive field binding rejects only ambiguous names. Reference.Bind and Schema.Select return ErrInvalidSchema when the requested case-insensitive name matches different field IDs, and the error includes both names. Unrelated names remain available to scans, writes, and schema, partition, and sort order updates. Delete files now have a separate 64 MiB target. Equality-delete and v2 position-delete files previously used write.target-file-size-bytes (512 MiB by default, or the table's override) as their file-size target. They now use write.delete.target-file-size-bytes, which defaults to 64 MiB. After upgrading, tables may produce more, smaller delete files unless this new property is set. To preserve the previous delete-file size target, set write.delete.target-file-size-bytes to the table's former effective write.target-file-size-bytes value (536870912 when the data-file target was unset). The data-file target itself is unchanged. Schema updates reject read-time type casts. UpdateSchema.UpdateColumn now allows only Iceberg schema promotions. Changes such as string to binary and fixed[16] to uuid are rejected by default. Schema reads now reject invalid identifier fields. Table and view metadata with identifier-field-ids referring to an optional, float/double, missing, non-primitive, or improperly nested field now fails to load with invalid schema (for example, invalid schema: identifier field "foo" must be required or invalid schema: identifier field "foo" cannot be float or double). Older iceberg-go releases could load such metadata, but Java Iceberg already rejects it. To recover an affected table, back up its metadata and use an atomic catalog metadata repair to remove the invalid identifier IDs or replace them with IDs of existing, required, non-floating primitive fields nested only in required structs. Do not edit the currently referenced metadata file in place. Repeated identifier IDs are deduplicated on read. Table history logs reject missing or null required fields. Loading table metadata now fails with table.ErrInvalidMetadata if a snapshot-log entry omits or sets snapshot-id or timestamp-ms to null, or a metadata-log entry omits or sets metadata-file or timestamp-ms to null. Older iceberg-go releases silently accepted omitted or null fields as zero values, but Java Iceberg already rejects such metadata. Explicit zero values remain valid. Repair affected metadata through an atomic catalog metadata replacement instead of editing the currently referenced metadata file in place. UpdateSchema rejects deleting an identifier field. DeleteColumn on an identifier column used to succeed and quietly drop the column from the table's identifier fields. Now Apply (and Commit) fails with cannot delete identifier field …, as in Java. Deleting a struct that contains one already failed, and now reports cannot delete field … as it will delete nested identifier field …. To delete the column anyway, also call SetIdentifierField with the identifier fields the schema should keep (for example SetIdentifierField([][]string{}) to clear them). This also stops a new column that reuses a deleted identifier column's name from becoming the identifier. Schema updates rewrite the table's name mapping. When a table has schema.name-mapping.default, every UpdateSchema commit now updates it, as in Java and PyIceberg; before, it changed only when WithNameMapping was passed. Added columns are mapped by name and renamed columns keep their old names, so data files without field IDs resolve them. If a new column reuses a name freed by DeleteColumn or RenameColumn, that name now maps to the new column: in older files without field IDs, the new column reads the values stored under that name, and a renamed column no longer reads them. Tables without the property are unaffected. Schema JSON defaults preserve integer precision. long defaults now decode as int64 instead of float64; non-integral, non-numeric, or out-of-range values now fail to parse. Numeric literals inside object and list defaults decode as json.Number rather than float64. REST mutation keys can enable transport replay. Namespace, table, view, transaction and scan-cancellation mutations listed in the REST catalog documentation now carry fresh UUIDv7 Idempotency-Key headers when GET /v1/config returns a non-null idempotency-key-lifetime. Go's HTTP transport may replay certain failed requests on reused connections with the same key; the advertised lifetime is not yet enforced. Scan plan and task key handling is unchanged. When a lifetime is advertised, a default Idempotency-Key configured via WithHeaders is dropped after GET /v1/config. StructType.Fields() returns a copy. Changing the returned slice no longer changes the struct, matching ListType.Fields() and MapType.Fields(). Build a new type with NewStructType instead. NumFields() and Field(i) read fields without copying, and NewListType and NewMapType are the constructors for the other nested types. The struct's field list is no longer exported; see the next note. Nested type fields are unexported. StructType, ListType and MapType can no longer be built with keyed struct literals, and their fields can no longer be assigned (see #2062 ). Build them with NewStructType, NewListType and NewMapType, and to change one, build a new value. Read them through methods named after the old fields: StructType.FieldList becomes Fields() (a copy), or NumFields() and Field(i) to read without copying. ListType.ElementID, Element and ElementRequired become ElementID(), Element() and ElementRequired(). MapType.KeyID, KeyType, ValueID, ValueType and ValueRequired become KeyID(), KeyType(), ValueID(), ValueType() and ValueRequired(). Schema.IdentifierFieldIDs is unexported too and becomes IdentifierFieldIDs(), which returns a copy. Set the IDs with NewSchemaWithIdentifiers, which keeps its own copy of the slice it is given. Pointers to these types and Schema encode to the same JSON as before. Values of these types, such as the result of Schema.AsStruct(), now encode like pointers instead of a partial form without "type", in which list and map values also dropped their element, key and value types. io.StatIO.Stat accepts a context. The method now takes a context.Context before the path, so custom StatIO implementations and callers must pass the operation context. Commits retry conflicts by default. commit.retry.num-retries now defaults to 4, as in Java and PyIceberg, so Commit refreshes and replays a conflicting commit up to four times before returning ErrCommitFailed. Set it to 0 to keep failing on the first conflict. table.CommitNumRetriesDefault changes from 0 to 4. The first Delete on a v3 table upgraded from v2 can fail with ErrCommitFailed. A merge-on-read Delete that gives a data file its first deletion vector now folds that file's v2 position deletes into the vector, so those deletes no longer reappear after the upgrade, and drops the file-scoped v2 position delete files in the same commit. Like any commit that removes delete files, it is not replayed: if another writer commits first, it returns ErrCommitFailed instead of refreshing and retrying. Reload the table and run the delete again. Partition-scoped position delete files stay in the table. Schema updates assert the last assigned field ID. When UpdateSchema adds a schema, the commit now also requires the table's last-column-id to match the transaction's base, as Iceberg Java does. A stale writer whose base predates another writer's column additions now fails with table.ErrCommitFailed instead of reusing field IDs. Reload the table and reapply the schema change. Schemas store binary and fixed defaults as hex strings. NewSchema, NewSchemaWithIdentifiers and UpdateSchema.AddColumn (through Apply()) convert []byte, BinaryLiteral and FixedLiteral defaults of binary and fixed fields, including fields nested in structs, lists and maps, to the lowercase hex string iceberg-go writes to metadata JSON, so a field read back from a schema holds a string such as "0aff". Code that type-asserts these defaults to []byte must decode the string instead, for example with hex.DecodeString. A schema built in process now equals the same schema read from metadata with lowercase hex. Equals compares the strings case-sensitively, and Java writes uppercase hex (see apache/iceberg#18352 ). The fields and types passed in are not modified. Predicates reject NaN literals when bound. EqualTo, NotEqualTo, LessThan, LessThanEqual, GreaterThan, GreaterThanEqual, IsIn, NotIn and LiteralPredicate/SetPredicate with a NaN float literal now fail in Bind with ErrInvalidArgument, as Java does. That includes the string "NaN" on a float column and a NaN on a decimal column, which used to bind as zero. Scans, ExpressionEvaluator and the metrics evaluators all bind first, so they return the error too. Use IsNaN and NotNaN to match NaN values. Out-of-range nanosecond timestamp strings are rejected. String literals for timestamp_ns and timestamptz_ns outside the signed 64-bit nanosecond range now fail expression binding with ErrBadCast. Scans and ExpressionEvaluator return the error for these filters instead of comparing a wrapped value. VisitBoundPredicateRef is removed. It was meant only for evaluators inside iceberg-go. Visitors in other modules should call VisitBoundPredicate, which passes VisitIn and VisitNotIn a detached copy of the predicate's literal set, as before. Empty string partition bounds are written as non-null bytes. New manifests preserve empty string lower and upper bounds, fixing filtered scans on identity partitions. Manifests written before this fix may retain null bounds for an empty string and can continue to skip matching rows until rewritten. Name mapping rejects ambiguous aliases and duplicate field IDs. Scans of files without field IDs now return ErrInvalidSchema when the same name belongs to multiple mapped fields at one level, instead of silently choosing the first. Repeated names on one mapping entry and same names under separate structs remain valid. Reusing a field ID returns ErrInvalidSchema instead of panicking. SQL view APIs align with catalog.ViewCatalog. CreateView now takes a *view.Version, schema and options, and returns *view.View. LoadView now returns *view.View; use Metadata() to access its metadata. If the caller leaves DefaultCatalog empty, SQL still sets it to the catalog name. LocationProvider.NewDataLocation takes the partition path. The method is now NewDataLocation(dataFileName, partitionPath string), matching Iceberg Java and PyIceberg, so custom LocationProvider implementations must add the argument. Callers pass the partition path there, or "" for an unpartitioned file, instead of prefixing the file name. Partitioned data files follow the table's location provider. With write.object-storage.enabled=true and the default write.object-storage.partitioned-paths=true, new partitioned files land under data/<hash>/<partition>/ instead of data/<partition>/<hash>/, which can affect prefix-based lifecycle rules and bucket policies. write.object-storage.partitioned-paths=false and write.data.path now apply to partitioned writes. Partitioned paths also no longer percent-encode the table location: s3://bucket/my table stays literal instead of becoming my%20table, as for unpartitioned writes. Existing files stay where they are. External object-store data paths include table context. For object-storage tables whose write.data.path is outside the table location, new data files now use <hash>/<db>/<table>/... after the shared storage prefix. This applies whether write.object-storage.partitioned-paths is true or false. The new prefixes may affect prefix-based lifecycle rules and bucket policies. Existing data files do not move. SQL catalog nested namespaces match the JDBC catalog. sql.Catalog.ListNamespaces(ctx, parent) returns only the direct children of parent, no longer parent itself or deeper descendants, and ListNamespaces(ctx, nil) returns the distinct first levels. A namespace that has no row of its own but has child namespaces, such as a after CreateNamespace(a.b), now exists for listing, CheckNamespaceExists, LoadNamespaceProperties, CreateTable, CreateView, CommitTable creating a table with AssertCreate, and as the target of RenameTable and RenameView; only CreateNamespace and UpdateNamespaceProperties still need its own row. DropNamespace returns catalog.ErrNamespaceNotEmpty while child namespaces exist. Walk the hierarchy one level at a time, and drop children before their parent. Catalog capabilities split into narrower interfaces. catalog.Catalog now embeds TableCatalog and NamespaceCatalog with unchanged table and namespace methods. Name() string is now required, breaking third-party catalogs and test fakes. ViewCatalog is optional (REST, Hive, and SQL), while REST, SQL, and Hive implement UpdatableViewCatalog for UpdateView. REST and SQL implement RenamableViewCatalog for RenameView. Use catalog.As[T](cat) and the Unwrap() Catalog convention to discover optional capabilities through decorators. Future capabilities should use optional interfaces rather than extending Catalog. Rename IO methods take a context. RenameIO.Rename and RenameNoReplaceIO.RenameNoReplace now take context.Context first, so custom implementations and callers must update. ReplaceFilesWithDeleteFiles removed. For delete-file replacements, use tx.NewRewrite(snapshotProps), call DeleteFile for each source file and AddDeleteFileWithDataSequenceNumber for each replacement, then commit the builder. Rewrites record a replace snapshot instead of overwrite. The five-argument ReplaceFiles API is unchanged and remains available for compaction and delete-file removals. Manifest and deletion-vector reads take a context. Snapshot.Manifests, ManifestFile.Entries, iceberg.EntriesWithProjection, dv.ReadDV and dv.ReadDVs now take a context.Context first argument and pass it to IO.Open. Custom ManifestFile implementations must add it to Entries. Path-based data-file addition renamed. Replace Transaction.AddFiles with AddDataFilesByPath, AddFilesOption with AddDataFilesByPathOption, and WithAddFilesConcurrency with WithAddDataFilesByPathConcurrency. Behavior is unchanged. Directory IO methods take a context. RemoveAllIO.RemoveAll and MkdirAllIO.MkdirAll now take context.Context first, so custom implementations and callers must update. Manifest builder constructor renamed. Replace iceberg.NewManifestFile(...) with iceberg.NewManifestBuilder(...). It still returns a ManifestBuilder. Manifest sequence APIs use explicit names. ManifestBuilder.SequenceNum and ManifestFile.SequenceNum become SequenceNumber, and ManifestFile.MinSequenceNum becomes MinSequenceNumber. ManifestEntryBuilder.SequenceNum and ManifestEntry.SequenceNum become DataSequenceNumber. FileSequenceNum becomes FileSequenceNumber for entries and their builder. Avro and JSON field names are unchanged. io.ReadFileIO.ReadFile accepts a context. The method now takes a context.Context before the path, so custom ReadFileIO implementations and callers must pass the operation context. View and UDF metadata builder constructors are infallible. view.NewMetadataBuilder and udf.NewMetadataBuilder now return only a builder instead of (builder, error); remove error handling at call sites. Table metadata getter renamed. Replace table.Metadata.Version() with table.Metadata.FormatVersion(), consistent with Iceberg Java and Go view/UDF metadata. Metadata JSON is unchanged. Snapshot ref type field renamed. Replace table.SnapshotRef.SnapshotRefType with table.SnapshotRef.Type. The JSON field is still "type". As-of snapshot lookups now use inclusive timestamps. Replace tbl.SnapshotAsOf(timestampMs, true) with tbl.SnapshotAsOf(timestampMs). The method always selects the latest snapshot at or before the timestamp, matching Java Iceberg's SnapshotUtil.nullableSnapshotIdAsOfTime. For strict-before lookup, use SnapshotLogEntryAsOf(tbl.Metadata().SnapshotLogs(), timestampMs, false). Snapshot timestamp property key corrected. PropertyCurrentSnapshotTimestamp now uses current-snapshot-timestamp-ms. The old current-snapshot-timestamp spelling is no longer reserved and remains usable as a custom property. FileIO open and remove take a context. io.IO.Open and io.IO.Remove now take a context.Context first argument, so custom io.IO implementations must add it. maintenance.WithCleanupDeleteFunc now takes func(context.Context, string) error. Hadoop catalog construction takes a context. hadoop.NewCatalog(name, warehouse, props) becomes hadoop.NewCatalog(ctx, name, warehouse, props). The context bounds filesystem setup; the catalog's filesystem keeps its values but not its cancellation. SQL and Hive catalog construction takes a context. sql.NewCatalog(name, db, dialect, props) becomes sql.NewCatalog(ctx, name, db, dialect, props), and hive.NewCatalog(props, opts...) becomes hive.NewCatalog(ctx, props, opts...). The context bounds the SQL table setup queries and is checked before the Hive metastore connect. Config loading reports errors. config.LoadConfig now returns ([]byte, error), and config.LoadConfigFile is removed; call LoadConfig instead. A missing default ~/.iceberg-go.yaml still returns no data and no error. Branch transactions return initialization errors. Table.NewTransactionOnBranch(branch) now returns (*Transaction, error), and Table.NewTransactionOnBranchWithError is removed. Use NewTransactionOnBranch and handle its error. Retries preserve staged update order. An append staged after RollbackToSnapshot stays on the rollback target after a retry or resumed Commit. If a staged update cannot apply after refresh, the transaction ends with table.ErrTransactionUnusable. For example, UpgradeFormatVersion cannot apply if a peer has committed a higher format version. The error preserves its cause and also matches table.ErrCommitFailed if that cause is a conflict. Previously, for transactions without a staged expiry, these failures returned table.ErrCommitRejected and left the transaction resumable. A catalog rejection on the first attempt still returns table.ErrCommitRejected and leaves the transaction resumable. Retries renew snapshot timestamps. A retry or resumed Commit stamps each snapshot it replays from a staged write with the current time, at least one millisecond after its parent, as Java's SnapshotProducer does. A snapshot staged more than a minute before a peer's commit no longer fails the retry. The committed timestamp is the time of the attempt that lands, so an ExpireSnapshots staged after the write in the same transaction keeps that snapshot when the commit retries. Snapshot expiration now tolerates concurrent ref changes. If a concurrent commit moves a ref that the expiry read, a retry or later Commit replans instead of failing with table.ErrCommitFailed. The committed expiry can differ from Transaction.StagedTable. See Snapshot expiration for cases that now fail with table.ErrTransactionUnusable. Snapshot expiration loads full REST history on demand. Expiration requests snapshots=all when a REST table was loaded in refs mode, including on commit retries. Use Transaction.ExpireSnapshotsWithContext to control the staging request. Catalogs that only supply refs-only history cannot safely expire snapshots. RowDelta reports a concurrent deletion vector as a commit conflict. If a concurrent commit adds a deletion vector for a data file that a RowDelta also adds one for, Transaction.Commit now fails with an error matching table.ErrConflictingDeleteFiles, table.ErrCommitFailed and table.ErrTransactionUnusable, and the transaction cannot be committed again. Previously, the error matched none of them and the transaction stayed usable. To resolve the conflict, reload the table and commit a RowDelta that adds one deletion vector merging the positions of both vectors and removes the concurrent one with RemoveDeletes. Schema JSON constructor uses the Go initialism. Replace iceberg.NewSchemaFromJsonFields with iceberg.NewSchemaFromJSONFields. AWS identifiers use the Go initialism. glue.AwsProperties, glue.WithAwsConfig and glue.WithAwsProperties become glue.AWSProperties, glue.WithAWSConfig and glue.WithAWSProperties; sigv4.WithAwsConfig becomes sigv4.WithAWSConfig; and config.CatalogConfig.AwsProfile becomes AWSProfile. The aws-profile YAML key is unchanged. utils is now awsconfig. utils.WithAwsConfig and utils.GetAwsConfig become awsconfig.NewContext and awsconfig.FromContext in github.com/apache/iceberg-go/awsconfig, with the same behavior. The utils package is removed. Remaining exported names use Go initialisms. table.PropertyUuid and table.PropertyCurrentSnapshotId become table.PropertyUUID and table.PropertyCurrentSnapshotID; table.ReassignedIds becomes table.ReassignedIDs; the table.WriteTask.Uuid field becomes UUID; glue.CatalogIdKey becomes glue.CatalogIDKey; io.ADLSSasTokenPrefix becomes io.ADLSSASTokenPrefix; and rest.Oauth2AuthManager and rest.NewOauth2AuthManager become rest.OAuth2AuthManager and rest.NewOAuth2AuthManager. The property and config key strings are unchanged. KMS factory registration now takes a context. Change encryption.KMSFactory implementations to accept (context.Context, map[string]string) instead of only properties, and call encryption.LoadKeyManagementClient(ctx, props) instead of LoadKeyManagementClient(props). The existing global RegisterKMS, UnregisterKMS, and GetRegisteredKMSNames functions still use the default registry; RegisterKMS still panics for invalid registrations. Use encryption.MustRegisterKMS for provider initialization. For isolated registrations, create registry := encryption.NewKMSRegistry() after importing any KMS providers and call registry.Register, registry.Load(ctx, props), registry.Names, or registry.Unregister. New registries snapshot the global registrations; subsequent changes do not propagate. Name-mapping child lookup renamed. Replace MappedField.GetField(name) with MappedField.FindFieldByName(name), which returns (*MappedField, bool). The new method returns a pointer to the actual child field rather than a copy, and reports a missing name with false. Data file block size setter removed. iceberg.DataFileBuilder.BlockSizeInBytes is removed. New v1 manifests use the Avro schema's 64 MiB default when the field is unset. V2/v3 omit this deprecated field, and legacy v1 values remain readable. View creation APIs take a named SQL representation. view.NewVersionFromSQL, view.CreateView, and view.CreateViewWithIOProperties now accept a view.Representation{SQL: sql, Dialect: dialect} instead of positional SQL/dialect strings. The dialect is required; Hive preserves the selected representation's dialect. View SQL representation construction uses named fields. Replace view.NewRepresentation(sql, dialect) with view.NewRepresentation(view.Representation{SQL: sql, Dialect: dialect}). Serialized JSON is unchanged. Hive views keep the caller's view version. hive.Catalog.CreateView now stores every representation, the summary, the default namespace and default-catalog as passed, instead of one representation with default-catalog set to "hive". Reserved table properties now use a read-only API. Replace references to table.ReservedProperties with table.ReservedProperties(). The function returns a fresh slice, so callers cannot change metadata validation by modifying it. Fixed and decimal constructors return errors. iceberg.FixedTypeOf and iceberg.DecimalTypeOf now return (type, error) instead of panicking for invalid inputs. Use MustFixedTypeOf or MustDecimalTypeOf only for known-valid values. SQL UDF representations now use struct literals. The udf.NewSQLRepresentation(dialect, sql) function, available since v0.7.0, is removed. Use udf.SQLRepresentation{Dialect: "trino", SQL: "x + 1"} instead. Empty fields and duplicate dialects are checked during metadata validation; serialized JSON is unchanged. Filesystem adapter construction consolidated. Replace io.FSPreProcName(fsys, fn) with io.FS(fsys, io.WithNamePreprocessor(fn)). Plain io.FS(fsys) remains supported. Table purge is required on catalogs. The catalog.Catalog interface now embeds catalog.PurgeableCatalog; every custom catalog implementation must provide PurgeTable(ctx, identifier) error. The narrow catalog.PurgeableTable interface is renamed to catalog.PurgeableCatalog. Built-in purge behavior is unchanged. Unify statistics blob types with Puffin. Replace table.BlobType with puffin.BlobType when constructing table.BlobMetadata. Replace table.BlobTypeApacheDatasketchesThetaV1 with puffin.BlobTypeDataSketchesTheta and table.BlobTypeDeletionVectorV1 with puffin.BlobTypeDeletionVector. Use puffin.BlobType.IsKnown() to identify the types defined by the Puffin specification; the redundant table.BlobType.IsValid() method is removed. Unknown non-empty blob type names still round-trip through table metadata. View representation field uses the Go SQL initialism. Replace view.Representation.Sql with view.Representation.SQL. Serialized view metadata still uses the sql JSON field. Orphan cleanup results now expose only OrphanFiles. Replace result.OrphanFileLocations with result.OrphanFiles (each entry has Path and SizeBytes). OrphanCleanupPlan.Files() still provides path-only lists during planning. Catalog identifier helper renamed. catalog.TableNameFromIdent is removed. Use catalog.ObjectNameFromIdent for tables, views, and functions. table/substrait is now internal. The package moved to table/internal/substrait, so substrait.ConvertExpr, substrait.ConvertSchema and substrait.NewExtensionSet are no longer exported. There is no replacement; scans and deletes still convert filters internally. Transform formatting requires the result type and uses the Java-aligned method name. Transform.ToHumanStr(value) and Transform.ToHumanStrType(resultType, value) are removed. Use Transform.ToHumanString(resultType, value) to format partition values, including timestamps with time zones. Year partition paths are zero-padded to four digits. YearTransform.ToHumanString now formats years below 1000 with leading zeros, as Java and PyIceberg do, so 0001-01-01 lands in ts_year=0001/ instead of ts_year=1/. New files for such partitions are written to a different directory than earlier iceberg-go releases used. Reads are unaffected because partition values come from manifests, not paths. Tooling that matches on partition paths should use the padded form. Catalogs now require cleanup. The catalog.Catalog interface includes Close() error. Custom catalog implementations must provide Close, and callers should close catalog instances after use. catalog.Closer is removed. Replace cat.(catalog.Closer) checks with defer cat.Close(); catalog.Catalog already implements io.Closer, so no type assertion is needed. table.ErrDataFilesMissing no longer matches table.ErrCommitFailed. An operation that adds delete files referencing data files that are not live, for example because a concurrent commit removed them, fails with ErrDataFilesMissing. The error is now terminal, like table.ErrCommitDiverged, matching Java's ValidationException, so code that retries when errors.Is(err, table.ErrCommitFailed) no longer retries it. When Transaction.Commit returns it, the error also matches table.ErrTransactionUnusable. Rebuild the delete against the current table instead. Puffin writer property setter renamed. puffin.Writer.AddProperties is now puffin.Writer.SetProperties. Repeated calls still merge keys; use ClearProperties to clear custom properties before finishing. Orphan file cleanup moved to table/maintenance. The orphan-cleanup and file-purge API is no longer on table.Table; it now lives in the table/maintenance package as free functions that take the table as their first argument (matching table/compaction). For example, tbl.DeleteOrphanFiles(ctx, ...) becomes maintenance.DeleteOrphanFiles(ctx, tbl, ...). Because table/maintenance imports table (and not the reverse), this cannot be offered as a deprecation shim on table.Table without an import cycle, so callers must switch to the new package. The following moved from table to table/maintenance: Functions (now free functions taking *table.Table): DeleteOrphanFiles, PlanOrphanFiles, ExecuteOrphanCleanup, PurgeFiles. Types: OrphanCleanupOption, OrphanCleanupResult, OrphanFile, OrphanCleanupPlan, PrefixMismatchMode. Constants: PrefixMismatchError, PrefixMismatchIgnore, PrefixMismatchDelete. Option constructors: WithCleanupLocation, WithCleanupFilesOlderThan, WithCleanupDryRun, WithCleanupDeleteFunc, WithCleanupMaxConcurrency, WithPrefixMismatchMode, WithEqualSchemes, WithEqualAuthorities. The four generic names (WithLocation, WithFilesOlderThan, WithDryRun, WithDeleteFunc) gained the WithCleanup prefix for consistency. Relatedly, the previously unexported isGCEnabled is now table.IsGCEnabled, so the new package can gate destructive operations on the gc.enabled table property. Metadata tables moved to table/inspect. Table.Inspect and InspectTable are removed. Each metadata table is now a free function in the table/inspect package that takes the table as its second argument, matching table/maintenance. For example, tbl.Inspect().Snapshots(ctx) becomes inspect.Snapshots(ctx, tbl). As with table/maintenance, table/inspect imports table, so table.Table cannot keep a deprecation shim. The following moved from table to table/inspect: Functions (now free functions taking the context, *table.Table and options): History, Snapshots, Manifests, Refs, MetadataLogEntries, Entries, AllEntries, Files, DataFiles, DeleteFiles, AllFiles, AllDataFiles, AllDeleteFiles, AllManifests, Partitions, PositionDeletes. Schema constructors: HistorySchema, SnapshotsSchema, ManifestsSchema, RefsSchema, MetadataLogEntriesSchema, EntriesSchema, AllEntriesSchema, FilesSchema, DataFilesSchema, DeleteFilesSchema, AllFilesSchema, AllDataFilesSchema, AllDeleteFilesSchema, AllManifestsSchema, PartitionsSchema, PositionDeletesSchema. Options: InspectOption is now inspect.Option, and WithInspectAllocator is now inspect.WithAllocator. DiffSnapshotFiles and ValidateSnapshot stay in table as Table methods: tbl.Inspect().DiffSnapshotFiles(ctx, from, to) becomes tbl.DiffSnapshotFiles(ctx, from, to), and tbl.Inspect().ValidateSnapshot(ctx, id) becomes tbl.ValidateSnapshot(ctx, id). ManifestProvider.UniqueManifests is newly exported for the all_* tables. Data-file replacement methods renamed. Use ReplaceDataFilesByPath for string paths. Use ReplaceDataFiles for prebuilt DataFile values instead of ReplaceDataFilesWithDataFiles. maintenance.PurgeFiles (previously Table.PurgeFiles) now calls IO.Remove concurrently, with up to 32 calls in flight, when the filesystem does not implement BulkRemovableIO. Custom IO implementations, including those registered with io.Register, must make Remove safe for concurrent use and synchronize any shared mutable state. The bulk deletion path is unchanged. Snapshot summaries report deletion vectors separately. On v3 tables, DVs are counted under added-dvs and removed-dvs instead of added-position-delete-files and removed-position-delete-files. added-files-size and removed-files-size use each DV's content_size_in_bytes instead of its whole Puffin file, so they go down for commits with DVs. total-files-size is updated from these values. Partition summaries, commit reports and OTel metrics change the same way. Existing snapshots are not rewritten. Deletion vectors identify row positions. New Puffin blobs list _pos field ID 2147483645 in fields, matching Iceberg Java. Existing files are unchanged. Partition and sort source accessors renamed. Replace PartitionField.SourceID() and SortField.SourceID() with FirstSourceID(). Their behavior and serialized fields are unchanged. Row-lineage column predicate renamed. Use iceberg.IsRowLineageColumn instead of iceberg.IsMetadataColumn to identify _row_id and _last_updated_sequence_number. Use iceberg.IsReservedFieldID to check the full reserved metadata field ID range. File writes and directory walks now take an operation context. Update WriteFileIO and ListableIO implementations and calls to Create, WriteFile, and WalkDir to pass context.Context; cloud writes and listings use it for cancellation. In and NotIn follow SQL semantics for NULL. A multi-valued NotIn, NOT(In(...)) and NOT(NotIn(...)) no longer match rows where the column is NULL, consistent with NotEqual. A predicate under NOT on a column missing from an older data file no longer matches every row of that file; those rows match as a stored NULL would. Java's Evaluator still matches NULL for notEq and notIn, see apache/iceberg#18701 . Commit rejections now match table.ErrCommitRejected. SQL, Glue, Hive and Hadoop failures while preparing metadata, plus REST commit responses 400, 401, 403 and 404, leave transactions committable (after a REST 404, the next Commit fails when it reloads the table). Existing errors.Is matches keep working, but SQL, Glue, Hive and Hadoop rejection messages now start with commit rejected: , so code that matches error text may need updating. Float comparisons against literals beyond the float32 range follow IEEE 754. On a float32 column, x < 1e100 no longer returns NaN, +Inf or NULL rows, and NOT(x > 1e100) no longer returns NULL rows. An infinite literal now binds to a float32 infinity, so x = +Inf matches +Inf rows. Java still folds these comparisons to always true or false, see apache/iceberg#18700 . Orphan cleanup refreshes metadata before deletion. Non-dry-run DeleteOrphanFiles requires a catalog-backed table and refreshes it before planning and again before deleting files. ExecuteOrphanCleanup also refreshes before deleting from a non-empty plan. If a saved plan is stale, refresh or reload the table before planning again. Dry runs still work without a catalog. Position deletes use the data file's partition spec. After partition spec evolution, Delete on a merge-on-read table wrote v2 position delete files with the current spec instead of the target data file's spec. Scans and re-running Delete on such a table can fail with invalid metadata: position delete file ... uses partition spec N, but data file ... uses partition spec M; some deletes are instead silently missed, so the rows stay visible, and re-running those deletes applies them. New deletes carry the data file's spec. For the mismatch error, remove the delete files whose spec ID differs from their data file's with Transaction.NewRewrite (RewriteFiles.DeleteFile), then re-run those deletes; until then the rows they deleted are visible again.

206.body:
If you would rather verify by hand, the underlying steps are: # Download the artifacts
curl -O https://dist.apache.org/repos/dist/dev/iceberg/apache-iceberg-go-${VERSION}-rc${RC}/apache-iceberg-go-${VERSION}.tar.gz
curl -O https://dist.apache.org/repos/dist/dev/iceberg/apache-iceberg-go-${VERSION}-rc${RC}/apache-iceberg-go-${VERSION}.tar.gz.asc
curl -O https://dist.apache.org/repos/dist/dev/iceberg/apache-iceberg-go-${VERSION}-rc${RC}/apache-iceberg-go-${VERSION}.tar.gz.sha512 # Verify the signature
gpg --verify apache-iceberg-go-${VERSION}.tar.gz.asc apache-iceberg-go-${VERSION}.tar.gz # Verify the checksum (or sha512sum -c on systems without shasum)
shasum -a 512 --check apache-iceberg-go-${VERSION}.tar.gz.sha512 # Inspect the archive, check licenses, and run the unit tests
archive="apache-iceberg-go-${VERSION}"
tar xf "${archive}.tar.gz"
( cd "${archive}" dev/release/run_rat.sh "../${archive}.tar.gz" go test ./...
) You should reply to the [VOTE] thread with +1, +0, or -1 and a one-line description of what you verified (for example, "verified signatures, checksums, and verify_rc.sh passed on macOS arm64").

iceberg-go registers the local file system (file://) automatically. Cloud schemes are not registered until you add a blank import: import _ "github.com/apache/iceberg-go/io/gocloud/s3" // s3, s3a, s3n, oss
import _ "github.com/apache/iceberg-go/io/gocloud/gcs" // gs

Importing io/gocloud registers all three at once and links all cloud SDKs. Without a matching blank import, these schemes return ErrIOSchemeNotFound with a hint naming the package to import. All credential and tuning property keys are constants in io/config.go . 22.body: When remote signing is disabled, authentication is resolved in this order (io/gocloud/s3/s3.go): Static credentials in properties: s3.access-key-id + s3.secret-access-key (+ optional s3.session-token). The standard AWS SDK v2 default credential chain - environment variables (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN), ~/.aws/credentials, container/IAM role. Tuning properties: Key (constant) Purpose s3.region (io.S3Region) / client.region (io.S3ClientRegion) AWS region. s3.endpoint (io.S3EndpointURL) Override S3 endpoint URL (custom or compatible storage). Falls back to AWS_S3_ENDPOINT env. s3.access-key-id (io.S3AccessKeyID) Static access key. s3.secret-access-key (io.S3SecretAccessKey) Static secret key. s3.session-token (io.S3SessionToken) Static session token. s3.proxy-uri (io.S3ProxyURI) HTTP proxy URL. s3.connect-timeout (io.S3ConnectTimeout) Either a number of seconds ("60", "60.0") or a Go duration ("5s"). s3.force-virtual-addressing (io.S3ForceVirtualAddressing) Force virtual-host-style addressing. s3.compat-mode (io.S3CompatMode) Enable for non-AWS S3 endpoints. Defaults to off. s3.remote-signing-enabled (io.S3RemoteSigningEnabled) Set to true to have a REST service sign S3 requests. Defaults to false. s3.signer.uri (io.S3SignerURI) Legacy signing service base URI. Requests use <base>/v1/aws/s3/sign. With remote signing enabled, S3 uses anonymous SDK credentials and obtains each request's signature from the signing service. No local AWS credentials are needed. REST catalogs use the table's /sign endpoint by default and pass through the response's remote-signing-config headers and properties. When that config is present, legacy signer.endpoint, signer.uri, and s3.signer.uri settings are ignored. rest.remote-signing.endpoint can explicitly override the default. It may be an absolute URL or a path relative to the catalog URI. Legacy settings are supported when the response has no remote signing config. A table-specific token takes precedence over the catalog token. The catalog's refreshing authentication is reused only when the signer shares the catalog's origin. For a separate signing service, use the headers supplied in remote-signing-config or a table-specific token. For a standalone S3 FileIO, set s3.signer.uri, s3.region, and an optional token for the signing service. When also supplying rest.remote-signing.config, set rest.remote-signing.endpoint to the complete signing endpoint instead. Object uploads use unsigned payloads. Only bulk-delete XML bodies are sent to the signer. Streaming signatures (aws-chunked) are unsupported. Caller-supplied checksum values are preserved; an upload that sets ChecksumAlgorithm must also supply its checksum value. Signing requests use the caller's context and a 30-second timeout unless the HTTP client has a configured timeout. Remote signing accepts a standard *http.Client or the AWS SDK's buildable client for S3 requests so redirects can be disabled. Other custom HTTP clients are rejected. S3 requests must resolve to SigV4; SigV4a and S3 Express signing are not supported.

24.body: Authentication is selected in the following order (io/gocloud/azure/azure.go); the first applicable option wins, and if none of 1-5 apply the default credential chain (6) is used: Shared key: a nonempty adls.auth.shared-key.account.name selects this path and requires a nonempty adls.auth.shared-key.account.key. Per-host SAS token: adls.sas-token.<hostname>, where <hostname> exactly matches the storage account hostname (for example, myaccount.dfs.core.windows.net). Per-account connection string: adls.connection-string.<account-name> (for example, adls.connection-string.myaccount). Static access token: a nonempty adls.token, supplied without the Bearer prefix. Managed identity: adls.auth.managed-identity.enabled set to exactly "true" selects this path and uses ManagedIdentityCredential directly. Set adls.client-id to select a user-assigned managed identity; otherwise, the system-assigned managed identity is used. Default credential chain: DefaultAzureCredential, which includes managed identity among its credential sources. adls.token accepts an OAuth2 access token for Azure Storage, including a token supplied by a catalog. An empty value is ignored. A rejected or expired token does not fall back to managed identity or the default credential chain. The token is static and is not refreshed. As in Java and PyIceberg , the credential reports a one-hour cache window to the Azure SDK each time the SDK requests the token. This does not extend the token's actual validity: Azure enforces its expiration. Callers must obtain a new token and recreate the FileIO when it expires; changing the original properties map does not update an existing FileIO. A REST catalog can also vend adls.token as a storage credential. The token carries no expiry of its own, so a vended token's expiry comes from expiration-time in the same credential when the catalog supplies one. Without it, a table FileIO that can fetch new credentials assumes a 60-minute lifetime and renews them shortly before it ends, and one that cannot, such as a FileIO for a scan plan's credentials, treats them as never expiring. A token whose actual lifetime is shorter than that fails with authorization errors until it is renewed, so catalogs that vend adls.token should send expiration-time with it. For the storage account it is vended for, a vended token replaces the SAS token and connection string configured for that account and any shared key, which would otherwise take precedence over it; a shared key is not scoped to an account, so one configured for another account would be used for this account too. The SAS tokens and connection strings of other accounts are kept. Expiries configured for other credentials, such as a SAS expiry or an expiration-time in the catalog or table configuration, do not affect when the token is renewed. Note on cross-client parity. The two properties in step 5 diverge from the other clients. adls.auth.managed-identity.enabled is Go-specific: neither Iceberg Java nor PyIceberg defines a property that forces ManagedIdentityCredential, so catalog properties that set it do not carry over. adls.client-id collides in name only — PyIceberg reads it as a service principal client ID used together with adls.client-secret and adls.tenant-id, neither of which iceberg-go defines (see the PyIceberg ADLS configuration ), while Java's AzureProperties defines no adls.client-id at all. Here it is only ever read as a user-assigned managed identity ID, and only when step 5 is selected. Tuning properties: Key (constant) Purpose adls.auth.shared-key.account.name (io.ADLSSharedKeyAccountName) Account name. adls.auth.shared-key.account.key (io.ADLSSharedKeyAccountKey) Account key. adls.sas-token.<host> (prefix io.ADLSSASTokenPrefix) Per-host SAS token. adls.connection-string.<account-name> (prefix io.ADLSConnectionStringPrefix) Per-account connection string. adls.token (io.ADLSToken) Static Azure Storage access token, without the Bearer prefix. Subject to the precedence above; not refreshed. adls.client-id (io.ADLSClientID) Client ID of a user-assigned managed identity. Used only when the explicit managed-identity authentication path is selected. adls.endpoint (io.ADLSEndpoint) Storage domain (e.g. blob.core.windows.net). adls.protocol (io.ADLSProtocol) http or https. adls.auth.managed-identity.enabled (io.ADLSManagedIdentityEnabled) Set to exactly "true" to use ManagedIdentityCredential directly, subject to the precedence above.

34.body: Key Default Description read.split.target-size 134217728 Target size for coalescing safe row-group ranges when splitting large local Parquet files. A range may exceed the target when no supplied offset can divide it safely. read.manifest-list-cache.enabled true Reuse decoded snapshot manifest lists across scans of a table handle. Set to false to disable retention and shared in-flight reads. Applied when loading or refreshing a table, and when creating a transaction scan. io.manifest.cache-enabled false Reuse raw manifest file content across local scans. Read from catalog FileIO properties in REST, Glue, SQL, Hive and Hadoop; REST table metadata and load-response config may override the catalog value. io.manifest.cache.expiration-interval-ms 60000 Idle expiration in milliseconds. Zero disables time-based expiration; negative or unparsable values warn and disable the cache. Expired entries are reclaimed on cache access/insertion, without a background cleanup task. io.manifest.cache.max-total-bytes 104857600 Retained raw bytes per independently loaded table. Handles returned by commit share their source table's cache and budget. Concurrent population buffers and bytes held by active readers are not counted. Non-positive or unparsable values warn and disable caching. io.manifest.cache.max-content-length 8388608 Maximum size of one manifest eligible for content caching. Non-positive or unparsable values warn and disable caching. The catalog's FileIO properties configure manifest caching for all built-in catalogs. With direct table.New calls, use WithScanPlanningIOProperties or WithSavedConfig; saved config wins when the same key is present in both. Matching expiration interval, total byte limit and per-manifest byte limit preserve warm cache entries across refresh and commit. Changing a limit replaces the cache. Unlike Java, which rejects invalid manifest-cache limits, Go warns and disables the content cache for negative or unparsable expiration or non-positive/unparsable size limits. The manifest-list cache retains at most 64 snapshots and 32,768 manifest descriptors in total per table handle. These are count limits, not byte limits: memory use also depends on manifest paths, partition summaries, and key metadata. Refreshing the table replaces its manifest-list cache. The optional manifest-content cache is separate. It stores immutable raw manifest bytes and still decodes, projects, and filters entries independently for each scan. Cache misses for the same manifest share one in-flight read. If population fails, its producer and each existing waiter independently fall back to one ordinary FileIO open; if the producer was canceled, live waiters can start another shared load. Failed content is not retained, so a later scan can retry. Manifests larger than the configured per-file limit bypass the cache. The current integration covers local scan planning; manifest lists continue to use the decoded manifest-list cache. The Java-compatible read.split.planning-lookback and read.split.open-file-cost names and defaults are also exported by the Go API for shared configuration, but are reserved for future task-group planning and are not currently read.

Bloom filters remain disabled for a column unless its enabled toggle is set. When adaptive sizing is enabled, an explicit column NDV takes precedence. Adaptive sizing rejects FPP values extremely close to 1 that could make the writer hang. Statistics settings apply to data files and use Iceberg field names, including nested paths such as items.element. Disabling statistics can reduce pruning and omit some Iceberg file metrics; other metadata may still be recorded. Floating-point Iceberg file metrics can also include NaN value counts. Column compression keys use case-sensitive Iceberg leaf paths, such as items.element or attributes.value.name. They apply to data files and use the global settings for columns without overrides. An explicit column level must be an integer valid for its effective codec. Missing fields are ignored. Parquet variant leaves do not have Iceberg field IDs and cannot be selected by these keys. Arrow does not register legacy lz4 or lzo codecs by default; lz4_raw is supported. Bloom column settings use Iceberg names, including items.element and lookup.value. Writers resolve these to the physical Parquet paths. Existing physical-path settings remain supported; logical names take precedence when both are present. Logical settings follow column renames and are removed when the column is deleted. Data-column Bloom settings do not apply to delete files. Equality-delete and v2 position-delete Parquet writers also support these overrides, defined in table/properties.go. Unset overrides inherit the corresponding write.parquet.* setting and its default. If the delete codec differs from the data codec and no delete level is set, the delete writer uses the codec's default level instead of inheriting the data codec's level. Key Overrides write.delete.parquet.row-group-size-bytes Row-group size target write.delete.parquet.page-size-bytes Data page size write.delete.parquet.page-row-limit Page write batch size write.delete.parquet.dict-size-bytes Dictionary page size write.delete.parquet.page-version Data page version: v1 or v2 (1 and 2 also accepted) write.delete.parquet.compression-codec Compression codec write.delete.parquet.compression-level Compression level As in Java, data-column Bloom filter and dictionary overrides do not apply to delete files. The global parquet.enable.dictionary switch still applies. Metrics configuration is independent: equality deletes use the table metrics settings, while position deletes always retain full file_path and pos bounds.

41.body: Key Description read.parquet.batch-size Arrow record-batch size used by the Parquet reader. read.parquet.max-compressed-page-size-bytes Maximum compressed page body. Explicit values must be integers from 1 to 2147483647, the largest size representable in a Parquet page header. Table properties apply to scans, deletes, delete-file inspection and maintenance. Two flags make these commands safe to run from cron jobs or CI: --yes skips the interactive prompt. Without it in a non-interactive environment, the CLI exits with stdin is not a terminal: use --yes to confirm in non-interactive mode rather than hanging. --output json emits structured output that can be consumed by jq and downstream tooling. On partitioned tables, files under older specs are preserved; only matching current-spec partitions are replaced. If the current spec is unpartitioned, non-empty input replaces all live files, including files under older specs. For v3, replacement also removes deletion vectors tied to replaced data files. Empty input leaves the table untouched. A concurrent add or removal in a replaced partition fails validation, while independent changes to other partitions can be retried after a catalog refresh. A new target branch also pins the source branch to prevent missing concurrent writes. Default partition-spec and sort-order changes fail validation. Written data files are not automatically cleaned up if staging or commit fails, so callers must handle those files before retrying with a new transaction.
